## About

I’m Dr Ian Henry and I live in a village just south of Cambridge. I am a licensed UK radio amateur and a member of [Cambridge and District Amateur Radio Club (CDARC)](https://www.cdarc.org.uk/), a friendly club which has been serving the Cambridge area since 1919.  I’m also a member of the [Radio Society of Great Britain (RSGB)](https://rsgb.org/) and write for their magazine [RadCom](https://rsgb.org/main/publications-archives/radcom/); my articles and talks are listed on the [Talks & Publications](talks.qmd) page.

I discovered amateur radio by chance in April 2025 and progressed through the Foundation, Intermediate, and Full licences within the same year, achieving my Full licence with distinction in December 2025. The pace of that journey reflects what I enjoy most about the hobby: learning, experimentation, and deepening understanding.

My interests centre on digital modes, SDR, and the theory that sits behind modern amateur radio practice. I spend a lot of time working with modes such as FT8 and JS8, [experimenting with packet radio](projects/gb7cam.qmd), and [building or configuring SDR-based systems](projects.qmd). I’m equally interested in how people learn these technologies and how we explain complex ideas clearly.

Alongside operating, I’m passionate about teaching, training, and helping others enjoy the hobby, particularly by demystifying the underlying concepts rather than focusing only on procedures or equipment.

That runs through everything here: writing that explains *why* things work rather than only how, and [projects](projects.qmd) that try to make the invisible parts of radio visible. The [home page](index.qmd) lists the sections of the site.

If you’d like to get in touch, collaborate, or talk radio, you can find contact details in the footer.
